newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran denounces U.N. human rights report as biased.
newsitem.headline: Iran denounces U.N. human rights report as biased.

text.p: Iran condemned as biased and unrealistic a United Nations report critical of the Islamic republic's human rights record.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi told Iran's official news agency IRNA on Thursday the report by U.N. investigator Maurice Copithorne reflected "the West's critical conception of Islamic values".

In a report for the U.N. Human Rights Commission released in Geneva on Tuesday, Copithorne implicitly rebuked Iran for maintaining a high rate of death sentences, for prosecution of religious dissidents, for killings of dissenters abroad, and for new pressures on the press.
He also said there was a "climate for change" in the status of women in Iran.

Mohammadi termed Copithorne's positive assessment of the situation of women in Iran as "something normal", but he regretted that the Canadian jurist had "filled the rest of his report with baseless rumours and false and unreliable accounts".

"Such biased and unrealistic reports not only mar cooperation between sovereign countries and envoys of the human rights commission but undermine the credibility of the reports of the rapporteurs and the concerned international organisations, including the Human Rights Commission," he said.

Mohammadi said "certain big powers" used human rights as a weapon against other countries. "Copithorne should not exploit the goodwill of Iran as an opportunity to contrast the outlooks of Western societies with Islamic values," he said.
Copithorne has been implicitly criticised by Iranian exiles for being "soft" on the Tehran government, but he argues that he presents the situation as he sees it.

However, the report, his third since he was appointed in 1995, revealed that he had been refused permission to go back to Iran late last year or early this year -- after a brief visit in February 1996 -- to gather fresh material for the new review.

The 53-member U.N. Human Rights Commission has repeatedly condemned the human rights record of Iran's Islamic government since it came to power in 1979 and is expected to repeat its condemnation in a resolution this year.
